claims.claimText: Under Columbia Law School's 2026–2027 Default Academic Policy on Student Use of AI (§9.1), use of AI during any examination is prohibited except where advance permission is granted in writing by the course instructor in the course syllabus and/or examination instructions; where not authorized, every word of an examination answer must be produced by the student without AI assistance (irrespective of whether proctored or take-home, online or handwritten), and students are strictly forbidden from inputting current examination questions, prompts, or fact patterns into an AI tool.

evidence.evidenceSnippet:
Examinations: Except where advance permission is granted in writing by the course instructor in the course syllabus and/or examination instructions, use of AI during any examination is prohibited.

- Every word of a student’s examination answer must be produced by that student without assistance from AI (including for English translation purposes). This prohibition encompasses all examinations, irrespective of format (i.e., whether proctored or take-home, online or handwritten).

- Students are not permitted to input current examination questions, prompts, or fact patterns from any course into an AI tool.

claims.claimText: Under Columbia Law School's 2026–2027 Policy (§8.3), students are permitted to consult AI to test arguments, solicit criticism, explore alternative articulations, and improve written work for clarity and reliability, alternate phrasing, and tone and concision, as well as identify and correct spelling and grammatical errors; in all cases students must exercise independent, rigorous critical judgment, and Sections 8–11 serve as default policies that instructors may vary in writing in the course syllabus or assignment instructions.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Writing Support and Error Correction: Students are permitted to consult AI to test arguments, solicit criticism, and explore alternative articulations. Students may also use AI to improve their written work, including for clarity and reliability, alternate phrasing, and tone and concision. Students are also permitted to use AI tools to assist in identifying and correcting spelling and grammatical errors. In all of these cases, students are required to independently and rigorously assess the feedback generated by AI, using their own critical judgment to decide whether and how to implement any suggestions.

claims.claimText: When an instructor suspects a student of using generative AI in violation of course policy, the instructor should refer the student to the Dean's Discipline process rather than attempting to resolve the matter independently.
